body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

clan_study | Narrator | - | The stones are cut in a script the party almost knows. One sentence.
clan_study_ok | Narrator | - | The names are Orc names, one clan, and they match the ones on the gravestone Yorgrim drags. One or two sentences.
clan_study_plain | Narrator | - | The names will not come clear. One short sentence.
lantern_statue | Narrator | - | A hooded figure carries a lantern in one stone hand; at its base a name has begun to etch itself. One or two sentences.
chamber_scene | Narrator | - | Inside the sepulcher, sconces of every colour burn down a long hall; the far end is collapsed, and grey mist wells through the rubble. Two sentences.
chamber_empty | Narrator | - | The beacon fires burn every shrouded away before they can rise; the hall is clean and silent. Two sentences.
chamber_good | yorgrim | smile | Yorgrim, quietly, says the friends' flames did their work. One short sentence.
chamber_spill | Narrator | - | Shrouded spill up out of the mist at the far end and the coloured flames burn some of them to nothing as they come. Two sentences.
rubble | Narrator | - | The collapsed passage is a wall of rubble and mist; clearing it will take time and hard work. One sentence.
rubble_ok | Narrator | - | Ten minutes of hauling stone and the passage opens onto a stair going down. One sentence.
rubble_slow | Narrator | - | An hour of sweat, but the passage opens onto a stair going down. One sentence.
maze_intro | Narrator | - | Passages fork in every direction, lined with grinning skulls; the floor trembles under a step here and there. Two sentences.
maze_hint_ok | Narrator | - | Faint candlelight winks in the eye-sockets of certain skulls, trailing off in one direction. One sentence.
maze_hint_plain | Narrator | - | The skulls grin and tell nothing. One sentence.
crack | Narrator | - | The floor is cracked and trembles under the party. One short sentence.
crack_ok | Narrator | - | A breach opens beside the party and they leap clear; a long way down, something shifts. One sentence.
crack_fall | Narrator | - | The floor gives way and the party falls sixty feet into darkness. One sentence.
depths_arrive | Narrator | - | A huge cavern widened by claws, slimed corpses in the burrows, and a heavy breathing somewhere above. Two sentences.
wall | Narrator | - | A cracked wall leaks grey mist; the party spots it and breaks through, and the stair's landing is on the other side. Two sentences.
slime | Narrator | - | A minute's careful work harvests a blob of necrolisk slime into a jar; it clings and eats at the glass. One or two sentences.
herb_mix | Narrator | - | The party mixes the lavender, lilies and nightshade into a stinking tincture that would make anything gag. One sentence.
necrolisk_ambush | Narrator | - | The great dragon-thing drops from a high burrow with a hiss. Two sentences.
stygian | Narrator | - | The Stygian Descent: a spiral stair carved with thousands of wailing faces, sconces burning the sick blue-green of the Shroud. Two sentences.
stygian_yorgrim | yorgrim | afraid | Yorgrim, thinly, says his light is dimmed here; the voices blame him in Common and in Orc. Two short sentences.
stygian_ok | Narrator | - | The party covers its ears and lets the wailing slide. One sentence.
stygian_fail | Narrator | - | The voices get in and will not be shaken for hours. One sentence.
tomb_door | Narrator | - | The doors are carved with a hooded woman holding a lantern. Only Yorgrim can open them. One sentence.
tomb_door_yorgrim | yorgrim | weary | Yorgrim, very faint, asks if they are ready. One short sentence.
tomb_open | Narrator | - | The doors swing in, and the cold of the Shroud rolls out over the floor. One sentence.
harrow_a | Narrator | - | The tear churns above the hanging platform; Yorgrim, translucent, raises his lantern into it. Two sentences.
harrow_b | yorgrim | afraid | Yorgrim, voice breaking, says the voices are saying his name. One short sentence.
harrow_c | Narrator | - | The lantern dims, a shrieking tendril wraps him, and a colossal hooded reaper stands in his place, scythe of blue-green fire, a gravestone on its back. Two sentences.
harrow_hold | Narrator | - | Yorgrim stands in the dark under the tear, his lantern raised. One short sentence.
azure_scene | Narrator | - | Where the Reaper fell there is only a big ornate lantern on the floor and Yorgrim's faint voice asking the party to perform his own rites. Two sentences.
result:
clan_study: The weathered markers are chiselled with jagged runes that tug at the edge of your memory, almost familiar under your tracing fingers.
clan_study_ok: They are orc names, all of the Shadestone bloodline. Every last one matches a name carved into the heavy slab chained to Yorgrim's back.
clan_study_plain: The mossy grooves blur beneath your thumb, refusing to yield their meaning.
lantern_statue: A cowled figure of grey stone holds an iron lantern out over the flagstones. Down at its plinth, fresh letters are slowly scratching themselves into the rock.
chamber_scene: Inside the sepulcher, wall sconces burn in five strange hues down a long, vaulted nave. The far end has caved in, and cold grey mist wells up through the fallen masonry.
chamber_empty: The newly kindled flames lick across the flagstones, searing every rising wisp of mist to ash before it can take shape. The long hall stands clean and dead silent.
chamber_good: Their fires hold the dark back, just as they promised they would.
chamber_spill: Gaunt, hollow-eyed spirits spill out of the seething rubble at the far end of the hall. The five coloured fires catch the foremost wraiths and burn them away like dry tallow.
rubble: Choking grey vapour curls through a solid wall of fallen lintels and wet earth that will take strong backs and bruised knuckles to clear.
rubble_ok: Ten minutes of heaving cold, slick stone opens a narrow gap onto a flight of steps descending into the dark.
rubble_slow: It takes an hour of aching backs and scraped palms, but the last boulder rolls aside to reveal a downward stair.
maze_intro: Narrow tunnels branch off in every direction, their damp walls mortared with rows of grinning, yellow skulls. Now and then the flagstones shudder beneath your boots.
maze_hint_ok: A pinprick of warm tallow light winks deep in the eye sockets of certain skulls, leading off down a single winding gallery.
maze_hint_plain: The rows of dry bone only grin back at you, hollow and unhelpful.
crack: Spiderweb fissures split the flagstones, and the floor shivers under your weight.
crack_ok: The stone splits wide beside your boots as you leap to solid ground, while something massive shifts in the black pit far below.
crack_fall: The rotten flagstones give way with a crack like thunder, dropping you sixty feet through the whistling dark.
depths_arrive: You stand in a vast cavern gouged wide by great claws, its earthen burrows choked with slime-coated bones. Somewhere high in the dark roof, something draws a wet, rattling breath.
wall: A hairline crack in the mortared stone weeps a thin ribbon of grave-mist. You put your shoulders to the rotten masonry until it gives way onto the lower landing of the stair.
slime: A minute of careful scraping coaxes a rope of pale, stinking necrolisk bile into a glass vial. It coils against the stopper, already etching frost into the jar.
herb_mix: You crush the dried lavender, graveyard lilies, and bruising nightshade into a thick, oily draught whose stench makes your eyes water.
necrolisk_ambush: Pebbles rattle down from a high burrow in the cavern roof. With a wet, rattling hiss, a scaled bulk drops out of the dark.
stygian: A spiral stair drops into the earth, its walls carved with thousands of open-mouthed faces that seem to breathe a low, endless moan. Iron cressets burn with the sickly blue-green tallow of the Shroud.
stygian_yorgrim: My lantern gutters in this air, friends. The dead know my voice, and they curse me in two tongues.
stygian_ok: You press your palms over your ears and keep your eyes on the steps, letting the cold wailing wash past like rain.
stygian_fail: The grieving chorus worms behind your eyes and sets your teeth chattering with a chill that will not leave for hours.
tomb_door: Twin doors of tarnished bronze bear the relief of a cowled woman lifting a lantern, sealed against every hand save Yorgrim's.
tomb_door_yorgrim: Stay close by me now, if you have the stomach for what waits inside.
tomb_open: The heavy bronze leaves swing inward with a groan, and the biting frost of the Shroud rolls out across your boots.
harrow_a: Above the iron-chained platform, the jagged tear in the world churns like a bruised storm cloud. Yorgrim, thin as smoke, lifts his iron lantern toward its roaring throat.
harrow_b: That is my clan crying out from the mist, and every mouth has my name in it.
harrow_c: The lantern gutters out as a shrieking rope of blue-green fog lashes around his throat. Where the old sexton stood rises a towering hooded reaper, a scythe of cold bale-fire in its fists and the chained headstone grinding against its spine.
harrow_hold: Yorgrim stands ankle-deep in the drifting frost beneath the tear, holding his dim lantern high.
azure_scene: Where the giant reaper came apart, only a heavy, soot-blackened lantern rests upon the cold stone. From inside its dark glass comes Yorgrim's faint, tired breath, begging you to read his last rites and let him rest.
